18:35.text: And he went into his garden while in a state
unjust to himself. He said: "I think not that this will ever perish.

18:36.text: "And I think not the Hour will ever come, and if indeed I am brought back to my Lord,
, I surely shall find better than this when I return to Him."

18:37.text: His companion said to him during the talk with him: "Do you disbelieve in Him Who created you out of dust
(mixed semen drops of male and female discharge)
, then fashioned you into a man?

18:38.text: that He is Allâh, my Lord, and none shall I associate as partner with my Lord.

18:39.text: "It was better for you to say, when you entered your garden: ‘That which Allâh wills
! There is no power but with Allâh
!’ If you see me less than you in wealth, and children,

18:40.text: "It may be that my Lord will give me something better than your garden, and will send on it Husbân
from the sky, then it will be a barren slippery earth.

18:41.text: so that you will never be able to seek it."

18:42.text: . And he remained clapping his hands
over what he had spent upon it, while it was all destroyed on its trellises, and he could only say: "Would that I had ascribed no partners to my Lord!"

18:43.text: And he had no group of men to help him against Allâh, nor could he defend

18:44.text: is the Best for reward and the Best for the final end.
(Lâ ilâha illallâh- none has the right to be worshipped but Allâh)

18:45.text: And put forward to them the example of the life of this world: it is like the water
which We send down from the sky, and the vegetation of the earth mingles with it, and becomes fresh and green. But
it becomes dry and broken pieces, which the winds scatter. And Allâh is Able to do everything.
